divergences.summary: Create New Budget seeds the previous release's schema without messages_pending; the pinned Actual creates it through migration 1788468782000.
PortableBudgetSchema.knownMigrationIDs lacks 1788468782000, so a new budget does not record it and Import Budget refuses archives from the pinned Actual; Actual records and accepts it.

An account close's transfer legs write isParent, parent_id, isChild, tombstone, error, and a null category cell that the pinned Actual does not emit; every oracle message is present. Causes: BudgetDatabase+TransactionCreation.swift:286-345 writes these cells unconditionally; BudgetDatabase+AccountLifecycleClose.swift:168 and :186 use it for both legs.

Rename refuses an exact duplicate of another account's name; the pinned Actual's handler accepts duplicates (its desktop UI validates separately). Cause: BudgetDatabase+AccountLifecycleWrites.swift:80 (duplicateName). Decision 2026-10-11: fix to match Actual.

Rename trims outer whitespace and writes nothing when the trimmed name is unchanged; the pinned Actual's handler writes every submitted value. Cause: BudgetDatabase+AccountLifecycleWrites.swift:66 (trim) and :72 (no change).
divergences.reason: User decision 2026-10-11: trimming and skipping an unchanged rename are harmless and intended.

divergences.summary: Reopening an account that is already open writes nothing; the pinned Actual emits another closed = 0 cell. Cause: BudgetDatabase+AccountLifecycleWrites.swift:100 returns noChange when the account is already open.

A due scheduled transaction posted after close or reopen omits the sort_order and reconciled cells that the pinned Actual writes, and writes default-valued description, category, notes, tombstone, isParent, and parent_id cells it does not. Causes: BudgetDatabase+ScheduleAdvancement.swift:204-214 builds the draft without sortOrder or reconciled; BudgetDatabase+TransactionCreation.swift:246-253 writes sort_order only when present; createSimpleTransactionMessages (TransactionGraphPlanning.swift:101) writes no reconciled cell.

Split diffs drop cells changed to null, 0, or false, and can emit an update with no cells. SplitTransactionFamily.swift changedValues (557-586) keeps only non-default values, so a child amount changed to 0 is missing from diff.updated, a final-child delete drops is_parent = false, and a child whose notes became null yields an empty update entry. The pinned Actual's getChangedValues (packages/loot-core/src/shared/util.ts) emits every changed key of the new object. Writes are computed from stored rows, so no sync defect follows from the diff shape.

Split conversion stores a zero sort order as 0 where the pinned Actual stores -1. The pinned Actual uses sort_order || -1 (packages/loot-core/src/shared/transactions.ts:387, where 0 is falsy); SplitTransactionFamily.swift:349 uses child.sortOrder ?? -1, which keeps 0. Affects family.children[0].sortOrder and rows[1].sortOrder.

Finishing reconciliation with a nonzero difference throws balanceChanged, where the pinned Actual records no error and locks zero transactions (nonzeroDifferenceLocks 0). Cause: BudgetDatabase+Reconciliation.swift:221-222 guards on canLockTransactions and throws. Expected output: reconciliation-contract.json, case finish.
divergences.reason: User decision 2026-10-11: telling the user the balance changed under them is safer than finishing silently.

divergences.summary: A balance adjustment whose rule clears notes still records the default note 'Reconciliation balance adjustment', where the pinned Actual leaves notes null. Cause: BudgetDatabase+Reconciliation.swift:140-141 restores the default note when the draft and preview notes are both nil.
divergences.reason: User decision 2026-10-11: the adjustment always carries its default note, even over a rule that clears notes.

divergences.summary: A balance adjustment whose rule deletes it writes no tombstone, where the pinned Actual's expected output records one deleted row. Cause: BudgetDatabase+Reconciliation.swift:130-135 returns committed false when the rule preview deletes the transaction. The delete rule is authored by the replay adapter (ReconciliationOracleReplaySupport.swift), so the expected deletion is a scripted outcome; see the README.
divergences.reason: User decision 2026-10-11: writing nothing is cleaner than a create plus tombstone; the end state is identical and adjustment rows carry no imported ID, so nothing dedupes against them.

divergences.summary: Unlocking a split member writes reconciled = false to each reconciled family row (parent and both children), where the fixture's expected rows record no reconciled write. Cause: BudgetDatabase+Reconciliation.swift:290-306 unlocks every reconciled row of the family. Whether the family should unlock together is a product decision.

A new income-carryover row's month identity is written as a number (N:202607), where the pinned Actual writes text (S:202607). Observable hold state matches under SQLite integer affinity. Cause: BudgetDatabase+BudgetWrites.swift:398-399 writes month as .int in budgetRowIdentityMessages, called from BudgetDatabase+HoldWrites.swift:122-124. The pinned Actual passes dbMonth(month).toString() in packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts resetIncomeCarryover.

API-level only; the menu never sends this reset. A reset-hold with no stored hold writes the income carryover rows, where the pinned Actual writes zero_budget_months buffered = 0. Cause: BudgetDatabase+HoldWrites.swift:44-55 runs resetIncomeCarryoverMessages when manualHeldAmount is 0 and writes the buffer only when it is nonzero.

A category with a null stored goal_def but a #template or #goal directive in its note gets no budget at apply; the pinned Actual regenerates goal_def from the note first, so the same case budgets it. Cause: BudgetDatabase+TemplateCategoryReads.swift:29-39 reads only stored goal_def and nothing regenerates it from the note at apply (called from BudgetDatabase+TemplatePreview.swift:354). The Swift replay that seeds the oracle's definition (replaysTemplateEngineWithStoredDefinitions) matches the oracle in every one of these cases, so the apply engine agrees once the definition exists. BudgetDatabase+TemplateNoteSync.swift:9 says Actualist applies CRDT-synced goal_def directly, so this may be a deliberate difference; the product decides. Up-to-date cases in this set produce zero messages, as the oracle does.
divergences.reason: User decision 2026-10-11: Actual is deprecating note-based templates, so Actualist does not support them; only stored template definitions apply.

divergences.summary: A stored template definition that no longer matches its category note makes the whole apply refuse, with no budget written in any category. The pinned Actual clears the stale definition and applies the other categories (tapply-named-stale-note-goal-def: Synthetic Rent's definition is cleared, Synthetic Groceries is budgeted 30000). Cause: the stale-note guard in BudgetDatabase+TemplatePreview.swift:378-392 throws unsupportedTemplate before any write, with the comparison from staleNoteManagedTemplateCategories (BudgetDatabase+TemplateNoteSync.swift:37). BudgetDatabase+TemplateNoteSync.swift:9-30 describes the guard as the safety half of Actual's preprocessing, so the refusal may be deliberate; the product decides. Once the refusal is removed, Synthetic Groceries also needs the OP-24 behavior.
divergences.reason: User decision 2026-10-11: refusing Apply Templates when a stored definition no longer matches its note is intended; the user resolves the mismatch first.

divergences.summary: A cover or transfer-available move writes the requested amount, where the pinned Actual clamps it: cover to the source category's leftover (actions.ts:549, min(abs(amount), leftoverFrom)) and transfer-available to To Budget (actions.ts:589, max(min(amount, leftover), 0)). Cover is reachable from the overspent menu. No app surface named transfer-available was found in Actualist/, so its reachability is unverified. Cause: no source clamp in OverspentCoverSelectionWorkflow.swift:72-84 (cover commands) or BudgetDatabase+BudgetWrites.swift:222 (moveMoneyMessages). Transfer-category is not clamped in the pinned Actual (actions.ts:643-670) and is not part of this entry. Includes downstream summary rows attributed by co-occurrence after the first divergent step. Decision 2026-10-11: fix to match Actual (cap Cover at the source's leftover and at To Budget).

A move to or from To Budget writes no <month>-to-budget zero_budgets row, where the pinned Actual writes one. Cause: moveMoneyMessages (BudgetDatabase+BudgetWrites.swift:222) writes no To Budget row. Includes downstream summary rows attributed by co-occurrence after the first divergent step.

A new assign or move budget row writes carryover = false, where the pinned Actual writes no carryover cell on that row. Analogous to OP-10 (extra cells on new rows). Cause: BudgetDatabase+BudgetWrites.swift:323-331 (assignCategoryBudgetMessages; move uses it at :276). Includes downstream summary rows attributed by co-occurrence after the first divergent step.

An existing budget row is rewritten with its category and month identity cells, where the pinned Actual writes none of them. Causes: budgetRowIdentityMessages callers at BudgetDatabase+BudgetWrites.swift:163 and :319, BudgetDatabase+HoldWrites.swift:122, BudgetDatabase+TemplateApply.swift:158. Includes downstream summary rows attributed by co-occurrence after the first divergent step.

A new budget row's month identity is written as a number, where the pinned Actual writes it as text. Same root cause as OP-20. Cause: BudgetDatabase+BudgetWrites.swift:398-399 (budgetRowIdentityMessages, also called from BudgetDatabase+HoldWrites.swift:122-124). Includes downstream summary rows attributed by co-occurrence after the first divergent step.

A reset-hold with no stored hold writes no zero_budget_months buffered = 0 row, where the pinned Actual writes it. Same root cause as OP-21. Cause: BudgetDatabase+HoldWrites.swift:44-55 runs resetIncomeCarryoverMessages without the buffered row when manualHeldAmount is 0.

A move or cover writes no 'Reassigned … from … on …' month note, where the pinned Actual writes one. Only the note's presence is compared; its date text comes from the fixture's fake clock and is not compared. Cause: no Reassigned writer exists in Actualist/. The move seam is BudgetDatabase+BudgetWrites.swift:210-240 and the cover commands OverspentCoverSelectionWorkflow.swift:58-84.
divergences.reason: User decision 2026-10-11: Actualist does not add automatic 'Reassigned' month notes on moves or covers.

divergences.summary: set-carryover carries through 12 months after the current date, where the pinned Actual carries through the budget's months (actions.ts:98 getAllMonths). Cause: categoryCarryoverHorizonMonth (LocalFirstActualStore+Mutations.swift:340-347). The replay fixes the clock at fixtureNow, so only cases whose horizon falls inside that window show this.

A manual hold is refused while the automatic income-carryover hold is active ('disable the automatic hold first'), where the pinned Actual commits the reset and then the hold and returns true. Open product question: whether the menu should allow a hold in this state. The guard was not changed. Cause: BudgetDatabase+HoldWrites.swift:21-22. Decision 2026-10-11: fix to match Actual (offer Hold; it replaces the automatic hold).

The exposed month value lastMonthOverspent is 0 in every month, where the pinned Actual exposes last month's overspend as a negative number when nonzero. Not displayed anywhere: no screen or widget reads the field, and To Budget is correct (it takes the carry-in from envelopeCarryIn). Cause: BudgetDatabase+BudgetReads.swift:53 hard-codes 0, while BudgetDatabase+EnvelopeCarryIn.swift:31-40 computes the value and discards it.

A set-account action is not recognised, so the whole rule is skipped: Actual stores the field as acct, and Actualist only accepts account. The rule's other actions are lost, and later rules that read the account see the old one. Cause: RuleAction.editorField/canRoundTripAndEvaluate (RuleRepository.swift:382-401) map only description to payee, so RuleConditionEvaluator.apply's account branch (RuleConditionEvaluator.swift:303) is unreachable for acct; conditions do map acct via RulePresentation.presentationField.

A delete-transaction action does not execute: Actual writes it as {op} with no value key, and Actualist's RuleAction requires one, so the rule fails to decode and the whole rule is skipped. Cause: RuleRepository.swift:156 (non-optional value in a synthesized Decodable), decoded with try? at BudgetDatabase+Rules.swift:223-225.

A set-notes action with an empty string stores nil, where the pinned Actual stores an empty string. Cause: stringOrNil (RuleConditionEvaluator.swift:341-344) maps empty to nil for every set action's text value.

A date condition with a recurrence value (schedule-style frequency, interval, weekend skip, end) never matches, where the pinned Actual matches the dates the recurrence occurs on, including the schedule rules that use them. Cause: compareDate (RuleConditionEvaluator.swift:234-236) requires both values to be strings, so an object value returns false.

contains, doesNotContain and matches on a payee condition compare the payee's display name, where the pinned runRules compares the payee id string (the name only matches in Actual's query path). Cause: RuleConditionEvaluator.swift:135-148 swaps the actual value to the name for id-typed fields.

Every ranked rule is a candidate, where the pinned Actual skips a rule that has both a payee and an imported-payee is, isNot, oneOf or notOneOf condition when neither index lists it. An or rule of two isNot conditions therefore runs in Actualist and is skipped in Actual. Cause: RuleConditionEvaluator.applying (RuleConditionEvaluator.swift:57) loops over all rules; Actualist has no equivalent of RuleIndexer.

payee_name is refreshed when a rule sets the payee, so a later payee_name condition sees the new payee's name, where the pinned runRules computes payee_name once before any rule runs. Cause: RuleConditionEvaluator.apply (RuleConditionEvaluator.swift:323-324) rewrites payeeName.

A rule that creates splits leaves the parent's payee as it was, where the pinned Actual clears the parent's payee (the children carry the payee). The preview cannot express clearing a payee at all: it reports nil for both unchanged and cleared. Cause: RuleSplitActionExecutor.swift:338-339 writes the parent record's payee back unchanged, and BudgetDatabase+Rules.swift:107 maps a cleared payee to nil.

transfer and parent conditions are evaluated against the draft's transfer and parent state, where the pinned runRules reads fields it never populates, so they match only when the input carries them. Cause: RuleConditionEvaluator.swift:121-122 with isTransfer/isParent set at BudgetDatabase+Rules.swift:635-636.

A rule linked to a completed schedule is skipped, where the pinned Actual still runs it (it is an ordinary rule once loaded). Cause: RuleConditionEvaluator.applying skips rule.isCompletedScheduleRule (RuleConditionEvaluator.swift:59).

A month or year upcoming length (for example "1-month") counts the days from today's date to the same date months later, where the pinned Actual counts whole months from the first of the month (on 2026-10-11 "1-month" is 32 days in Actual and 42 in Actualist), so schedules near the edge of the window get a different upcoming/scheduled status. Cause: ScheduleUpcomingLength.swift:36-41 adds the months to today's date, where getUpcomingDays adds them to a month string and counts calendar days from the month start.

Skipping a schedule that moves weekend dates before, from a Friday next date, starts the search the day after the following Monday, so an occurrence that falls on that Monday is passed over (the pinned getNextDateAfter returns it). Cause: ScheduleRuleMutation.nextDateAfterSkip (ScheduleRuleMutation.swift:186-196) moves the start to Monday and then adds a day.

Automatic advancement of a schedule that moves weekend dates before never leaves a Friday that stands in for a Saturday or Sunday occurrence: the next date stays on that Friday while the pinned advancement moves to the next date after it, so later occurrences are never posted. Cause: advancedRecurringDayID (BudgetDatabase+ScheduleAdvancement.swift:286-294) searches from the day after the Friday, whose occurrence maps back to the same Friday, so advanced == effective at :258 and the date is left unchanged; Actual's getNextDateAfter retries past such occurrences.

A paid recurring schedule that does not post transactions moves to the occurrence right after the paid one, where the pinned Actual recomputes its next date from today and so passes over every missed occurrence in between. Cause: ScheduleOccurrencePlanner.swift:42-44 returns advanceRecurring for that branch, and advanceRecurringOccurrence (BudgetDatabase+ScheduleAdvancement.swift:229-298) moves one occurrence from the day after the current date; Actual calls setNextDate without advance there.

A schedule whose amount is a between range stored high to low (for example -10,001 and -200.00 as num1 and num2) is treated as unsupported, so automatic posting refuses it, where the pinned Actual posts the rounded average of the two values. Creating such a schedule is refused too. Cause: ScheduleRuleProjection.amount(from:) requires lower <= upper (ScheduleRuleProjection.swift:232) and ScheduleRuleMutation.amountValue rejects the range at :308.

Skipping the next date of a one-time schedule is refused with an unsupported-capability error, where the pinned Actual accepts the skip and leaves the schedule unchanged. The stored result is the same. Cause: canSkip requires a recurrence (ScheduleRuleProjection.swift:105) and prepareScheduleSkip throws at BudgetDatabase+ScheduleWrites.swift:310-312.
divergences.reason: User decision 2026-10-11: Actualist hides Skip Next Date for one-time schedules, so the refusal is unreachable from the UI and the saved data is identical; Actual's menu offers a skip that does nothing.

divergences.summary: A schedule created on a day gets its first next date from that day, where the pinned Actual searches from the day before in a time zone behind UTC (a daily-every-3-days schedule from 2026-10-01 created on 2026-10-11 in America/New_York starts on 2026-10-10 in Actual and 2026-10-13 in Actualist). Cause: Actual's createSchedule calls getNextDate with the default start new Date(currentDay()), which parses the day as UTC midnight; Actualist's ScheduleRuleMutation.initialNextDate (ScheduleRuleMutation.swift:172) starts at the given day. Not the cause of OP-13.
divergences.reason: User decision 2026-10-11: keep the local creation day. Actual's UTC parse of the creation day looks like an upstream bug that can start a new schedule a day early west of UTC; both apps read the stored next date afterwards.

divergences.summary: Creating a schedule on a closed account is refused ("Choose an available, open account for this schedule."), where the pinned Actual's createSchedule accepts any account in the rule. Actual's own editor does not offer closed accounts, so this is an API-level difference. Cause: validateScheduleAccount rejects a closed or deleted account (BudgetDatabase+ScheduleWrites.swift:412-420).
divergences.reason: User decision 2026-10-11: keep refusing closed accounts at create. Neither app's editor offers a closed account, and advancement of an existing schedule on a closed account already matches Actual.
